messages:
incidents-bot: Pager: Elevated 5xx error rate (inference RPC failures) from ca-central-1a. Context: NLB target group health flapping + DNS resolver timeouts. P90 latency spiking for dedicated pools in ca-central-1a. Paging @dana-oncall :rotating_light:

Dana-oncall: saw it. joining. what svc/stack is primary?

Bob-sre: this looks like network egress path errors from the AZ. NLB metrics show high connection reset counts and instance-level ENI rx drops. Happening ~ 05:10 UTC.

Charlie-net: I see control-plane DNS resolver (VPC resolver) in ca-central-1a returning SERVFAIL intermittently. That would make model lookup / variant resolution fall back and cause retries.

Dana-oncall: customers impacted? any user-facing rate?

Evan-prod: quick check: Dedicated customers pinned to ca-central-1a show 12-18% 5xx rate over last 20m, and p50/p90 token latencies up from 60ms to 420/980ms respectively. Hosted API (multi-az) auto-steering mitigated most traffic but some sticky sessions still hitting the zone.

Maya-eng: KV cache misses shot up — I think many requests are getting TTL misses due to resolver failures, forcing prefix cache refreshes -> higher token/sec CPU.

Dana-oncall: ok first-step mitigation list: 1) divert new traffic away from ca-central-1a (weighting) 2) decrease retry aggressiveness/circuit-break 3) drain target group members in that AZ 4) notify customers and set status page

Bob-sre: on (1) — For hosted/primary routing we can adjust Route53 weighted failover to send 90% of traffic to ca-central-1b/c. I'll make a small change so clients without sticky cookies see same behaviour. For Dedicated, we need to reassign capacity via control-plane route rules.

Charlie-net: I can flip regional resolver settings to prefer cross-AZ resolver endpoints, but DNS TTLs are low (30s) so rotation will be quick.

Dana-oncall: do it. Bob, can you also reduce health-check dereg delay so target group drains faster?

Bob-sre: setting target group deregistration delay to 10s for affected TGs now. command: 

```
aws elbv2 modify-target-group-attributes --target-group-arn arn:aws:elasticloadbalancing:ca-central-1:xxx:targetgroup/tg-infer-1 --attributes Key=deregistration_delay.timeout_seconds,Value=10
```

Bob-sre: done for tg-infer-1/tg-infer-2. Starting a scripted drain of instances in ca-central-1a (will keep retry budget low).

Maya-eng: lowering client retry multiplier on the router (no backoff to 1.5x -> 1x) in prod router config to avoid amplifying failures. pushing patch now.

Dana-oncall: Charlie — proceed with resolver preference flip and set cross-zone resolver TTL to 5s? is that possible?

Charlie-net: we can add Route53 resolver endpoint priority change and update Route53 inbound endpoints. I'll add higher weight to resolver endpoints in other AZs. Not changing TTLs globally. Rolling now.

ops-bot: change-request: route53-weight-update initiated by bob-sre. ChangeId: r53chg-20475-01

Bob-sre: applying weighted record set change: sending 85% to ca-central-1b/15% to ca-central-1c for the inference api R53 entry. snippet: 

```
aws route53 change-resource-record-sets --hosted-zone-id ZZZZZ --change-batch '{"Changes":[{"Action":"UPSERT","ResourceRecordSet":{"Name":"infer.api.redwood.internal.","Type":"A","SetIdentifier":"ca-central-1b","Weight":85,"TTL":30,"ResourceRecords":[{"Value":"10.2.3.11"}]}}]}'
```

Bob-sre: applied. Should see traffic shift within one TTL (~30s).

Evan-prod: starting status update draft: "We are investigating elevated error rate impacting customers pinned to ca-central-1a. Mitigations in progress: diverting new traffic, draining affected nodes, and lowering retry budgets. More to follow." Any additions?

Dana-oncall: add: "no data exfiltration observed, serving degraded for small subset of Dedicated customers; hosted generally ok."

Maya-eng: small note — to reduce latency impact we can temporarily route certain critical customers to smaller model variants (latency-optimized) while we rebalance. Would need product signoff, but we can opt-in via per-customer routing override.

Evan-prod: good idea. I'm drafting message to affected customers offering optional switch to latency mode.

Charlie-net: I see resolver error rate dropping after reroute. NLB resets are still elevated on a tiny subset — likely instance NIC queue saturation. I've opened a support case with AWS (case #1234567890).

Dana-oncall: handing off to bob-sre for active mitigation and follow-up. If any blocker escalate to oncall page. Hand-off time 2047501300.

Bob-sre: taking it. I'll keep this thread updated. Current status: traffic diverted ~85% away, drain in progress, retries lowered. Monitoring p95/p99 for errors and latency.

ops-bot: incident-ref: INC-2047501110 created, severity: high, owner: bob-sre

Bob-sre: observing error rate down from 18% -> 6% within 4m. Sticky sessions shaved off via cookie invalidation on the router for affected pools. Command used: 

```
curl -X POST -H "Authorization: Bearer $ADMIN_TOKEN" https://router.internal/clear-session-cookies -d '{"pool":"ca-central-1a-infer"}'
```

Maya-eng: KV cache miss rate dropping. prefix cache warmups finished on new AZ targets.

Evan-prod: status page update posted. Customers notified via email draft (will send to Dedicated customers pinned to ca-central-1a).

Charlie-net: AWS confirmed ENI device queue saturation due to noisy flow from a customer-managed VPCAttach. AWS is throttling that interface — they're working on mitigation. They recommend spreading traffic (we introduced weighted routing).

Bob-sre: marking incident as mitigated. Will keep monitoring for 1h. Follow-ups: 1) AWS case action items, 2) add resolver health checks that track SERVFAIL rate and trigger auto-steering earlier, 3) review target group dereg delay defaults, 4) run chaos test for resolver failure in staging.

Maya-eng: I'll run an evaluation to see if routing to smaller model variant caused any quality regressions.

Evan-prod: drafting post-incident summary for customers + internal RCA template.

Dana-oncall: thanks all. If error creeps back -> page oncall. For now I'll close pager but keep watch. :white_check_mark: 

ops-bot: incident INC-2047501110 status updated -> mitigated (2047502820)

Bob-sre: final note: root cause likely localized ENI/egress saturation in ca-central-1a leading to DNS resolver timeouts and NLB connection resets. AWS support assigned follow-up.

Maya-eng: created follow-up ticket in backlog: INFRA-3297 (resolver health checks + per-AZ throttling alarms).

Evan-prod: closing with customer messaging scheduled. Good work everyone. :clap:
